Banks and other sensitive apps block phones that have an active accessibility service (anti-fraud). To avoid that, this app turns itself off when it detects one, so you\'re never blocked. A reminder notification lets you turn it back on with one tap when you\'re done.
Turn off automatically for sensitive apps

Grace period after you leave a sensitive app, so hopping back in doesn\'t find an active accessibility service. Going back during the wait cancels it, and opening the Camera turns Video Boost on right away.
The service turns off automatically when a checked app opens. Banks and other sensitive apps are checked by default; uncheck any you don\'t want, or check more below.

Reminds you on the app opening. Tap to set up more.

By default the reminder shows when a sensitive app opens. With monitoring, the notification is silent while the app is open and only alerts you when you close it. With Shizuku, Video Boost also turns itself back on automatically — no tapping.

Get the free Shizuku app from the Play Store or its website.
Open Shizuku and start it via wireless debugging (Android 11+), a computer with ADB, or root. Shizuku\'s own guide walks you through it. You may need to restart it after a reboot.
Come back here, flip “Full-auto (Shizuku)” above and allow the permission Shizuku asks for. Done — Video Boost now handles sensitive apps by itself.
Wireless ADB paired and full-auto on.
Paired. Re-enable wireless debugging after a reboot, then reconnect.
Pair once to enable and re-enable Video Boost without Shizuku.

Instead of installing Shizuku, Video Boost can talk to your phone\'s own “Wireless debugging” directly. Pair once and it can turn its accessibility service on and re-enable it after a sensitive app closes — no second app.
In Developer options, turn on “Wireless debugging”. (Enable Developer options first by tapping the build number 7 times.)
Tap below, then open “Pair device with a pairing code”. A notification will pop up where you type the 6-digit code — so you never have to leave the pairing screen.
Now open Wireless debugging → “Pair device with a pairing code”. A notification will ask for the code — type it there without leaving that screen.
After a reboot you must re-enable “Wireless debugging” once; then tap Reconnect. No new code is needed.

Couldn\'t connect. Make sure “Wireless debugging” is on.

Video Boost processes video in the cloud through Google Photos. Each video is stored twice and uses data. Always-on means more of both.
Two ways to run it. Always-on works on any phone; on-demand keeps the accessibility service switched off except while the Camera is open, and needs the special ADB permissions.
The accessibility service stays enabled and filters events in code. No special permissions, but sensitive apps force it to turn itself off.
The service stays off and switches itself on the moment Pixel Camera comes to the front, then off again when you leave. Banks never see it running, so there is nothing to turn off for them.

Needs two special permissions: “Usage access” to notice the Camera opening, and local write access to switch its own service. Pair wireless ADB (or Shizuku) from the wireless ADB screen and the app grants them to itself, once.

Grace period so hopping out to the gallery and back does not switch the service off and on again. A sensitive app in the foreground cuts it short and switches off at once.
The service is off right now. It turns on by itself while the Camera is open and off again when you leave.
On-demand mode needs the special ADB permissions. Grant them in “How it turns on”, or switch back to always-on.
In on-demand mode the service only exists inside the Camera, so a bank never runs alongside it. This section comes back if you switch to always-on.

No ads, no tracking, no accounts. If this app saves your videos, you can support its development — it helps keep it working after every Pixel Camera update.
What it does exactly, every permission explained

It watches for Pixel Camera in video mode. When it appears, it opens the Video Settings panel, reads the real state of the Video Boost toggle, turns it on only if it is off, and closes the panel — about half a second. That is all. It only reads and taps controls inside Pixel Camera; events from other apps are used solely to notice that the Camera left the screen or that a sensitive app opened, and are discarded on the spot.

It never reads or stores what is on your screen, never collects data, and has no analytics, no ads and no accounts. Nothing leaves your phone: the only network use is checking GitHub for new versions (and, if you enable it, the wireless-ADB connection to your own phone over localhost).
The complete source code is public. Anyone can read it, audit it or build the APK themselves — you do not have to take anyone\'s word for any of this.
View the source code on GitHub

The only way to flip a switch inside another app without root. Android warns about it because a malicious app could abuse it; here it only touches Pixel Camera, and the code is open so you can verify that.
Used for exactly one thing: asking GitHub whether there is a newer version. No other traffic, ever.
The reminders and confirmations you control in the Notifications screen. Every optional one can be switched off.
What Android requires while the app waits for a sensitive app to close or for the Camera to open (on-demand mode). Its notification is required by the system; it can be silenced.
Only if you enable full-auto or on-demand mode: lets the app see which app is in the foreground, locally, so it knows when the Camera opens or a sensitive app closes. Nothing is recorded anywhere.
Granted only by you, through wireless ADB or Shizuku: lets the app switch its own accessibility service on and off — the same command you would type over ADB, nothing else.
Why it is not on the Play Store

Play\'s policy forbids using accessibility to automate another app, which is this app\'s whole purpose. That is also why Play Protect warns when you install the APK: it flags every sideloaded accessibility app, and it does not mean something is wrong. Distribution is through GitHub Releases and Obtainium instead.
Works on Pixel Pro models with Video Boost (Pixel 8 Pro and newer Pro models).
